2027-01-16.title: Saturday of the First Week in Ordinary Time
readings: The word of God is living and active
Your words, Lord, are Spirit and life
I have come to call not the righteous but sinners
2027-01-16.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 1 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green. In India: St Joseph Vaz, priest (check the diocesan calendar). Optional: Saturday memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary.
2027-01-16.verse: Indeed, the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing until it divides soul from spirit, joints from marrow; it is able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
theo: Hebrews offers two images side by side. First, the word of God is “living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword”: it reaches the hidden places of the heart and lays everything bare. That could frighten us. But immediately comes the second image: “we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but we have one who in every respect has been tested as we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore approach the throne of grace with boldness.” The word that sees everything leads us to the mercy that forgives everything.

Mark shows this in action. Jesus sees Levi sitting at the tax booth, a collaborator despised by his people, and says: “Follow me.” Levi gets up and follows, and soon Jesus is eating at his table with “many tax collectors and sinners”. The Pharisees are shocked. Jesus answers: “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick; I have come to call not the righteous but sinners.” The Church is first a hospital for sinners, and every one of us is a patient called to follow.
outline: Ask: when has a word of Scripture cut to your heart?
“I have come to call not the righteous but sinners.”
live: Read today's Gospel slowly and ask: what does it reveal in my heart?
Share a meal or tea with someone others look down on.
2027-01-16.prayer: Lord Jesus, your word is living and sees my heart, and you are a high priest who understands my weakness. Call me again as you called Levi, heal me as the doctor of sinners, and let me approach your throne of grace with confidence. Amen.
altar: At Mass the word of God is proclaimed, and then the Physician of souls feeds us at his table. Like Levi's guests, we come as sinners and are welcomed.

quick: God's word is living and sees the heart.
Jesus calls Levi and eats with sinners.
We approach the throne of grace with boldness.
2027-01-16.action: Share a meal or tea with someone others look down on.
2027-01-16.question: Do I see the Church as a hospital for sinners, including me?

family.explain: Levi was a tax collector, and people did not like him. Jesus said: follow me! Then Jesus ate with Levi and his friends. Jesus came to help those who need him.
family.intention: We pray for people who feel others look down on them.
family.ask: Ask: “Who could we invite to our home or our table?”

illus: A parish in Ernakulam began a monthly Sunday lunch to which everyone was invited: families, migrant workers, a few men from the bus stand. At first some parishioners grumbled. A year later one of the men from the bus stand was serving at the tables. The parish priest said: this is what Jesus did at Levi's house.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, your word is living and active. Speak to our hearts as we gather, and welcome us as you welcomed Levi. Amen.
share: The word of God is living and active (Hebrews 4:12). What has God's word shown me lately?
Follow me (Mark 2:14). What is my tax booth?
Approach the throne of grace with boldness (Hebrews 4:16). Do I come to God with confidence?
pm.resp: Lord, have mercy on us sinners.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a home for sinners.
For tax collectors, officials and all handling public money, that they may be honest.
For those who feel unworthy of God.
For priests in the confessional, ministers of the throne of grace.
For our group, that we may welcome all as Jesus did.
pm.close: Father, your Son called Levi and ate with sinners. Let your word search our hearts and your mercy heal them. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews gives us a strong image: the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword; it is able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart (Hebrews 4:12). God's word sees us as we are.

That could frighten us. But Hebrews continues: we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but one who in every respect has been tested as we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore approach the throne of grace with boldness (Hebrews 4:15–16).
In the Gospel Jesus sees Levi at the tax booth. Tax collectors worked for the Romans and were often dishonest. People despised them. Jesus simply says: follow me. And Levi gets up and follows.

Then Jesus eats at Levi's house with many tax collectors and sinners. The Pharisees complain. Jesus says: those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick; I have come to call not the righteous but sinners (Mark 2:17).

The Church is a hospital for sinners. Let God's word show us our sickness, and let us come boldly to the throne of grace for healing. On this Saturday let us also ask Mary, Refuge of sinners, to bring us to her Son. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus called Levi, whom nobody liked, to be his friend. Jesus loves everyone. Let us be friends with someone who has no friends.

intro: Theme: “I have come to call not the righteous but sinners.”
The word that searches the heart and the mercy that welcomes the sinner.

q: Is not my word like fire, says the LORD, and like a hammer that breaks a rock in pieces?

Indeed, the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing until it divides soul from spirit, joints from marrow; it is able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
points.apply: Pray with today's Gospel for ten minutes.

q: For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.
When Jesus heard this, he said to them, “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick; I have come to call not the righteous but sinners.”

sub: Tested as we are, without sin.
q: As a father has compassion for his children, so the LORD has compassion for those who fear him.
Let us therefore approach the throne of grace with boldness, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need.

concl: The word shows our sickness; the Physician heals it.
Come boldly: the throne is a throne of grace.
2027-01-16.resolve: Read one Gospel passage each day and let it search your heart.
